st.headline: Partners Group exits bubble-tea brand Gong Cha after Bain buyout
st.teaser: Partners Group in 2019 provided more than US$200 million to support TA Associates’ acquisition of Gong Cha.
fullText: Partners Group will exit its private credit investment in Gong Cha after Bain Capital bought the Taiwanese bubble-tea brand from TA Associates in August.
The Swiss-based private asset manager said it has entered an agreement to be fully repaid, according to a document seen by Bloomberg.
Partners Group in 2019 had provided a financing package of more than US$200 million (S$254 million) to support TA Associates’ acquisition of Gong Cha and also took a minority equity stake.
The returns on the investment were not disclosed.
While private credit is growing in Asia Pacific, the region that still makes up only a small portion of the global US$1.8 trillion market.

Its immediate outlook also faces a number of challenges. Economic uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, and elevated interest rates are set to slow growth in private credit fundraising in the region as investors become more wary of illiquid assets, Moody’s Ratings said in a report in July.

While exiting its Gong Cha position, Partners Group is seeking further investment opportunities in Asia, as its customers look to diversify away from the US, global head of private debt Andrew Bellis said in an interview recently.

The asset manager has already deployed several billion dollars in Asia across more than 50 private credit investments over the past 15 years, with most of those in the past five to seven years, he said.
“What we’re seeing is more clients looking to make dedicated allocations to Asia private credit,” Bellis said.

Partners Group recently closed a US$1 billion private credit mandate with a major institutional investor in Asia, including a discretionary tranche that it will manage as well as co-investment capital, it announced. The company currently oversees about $6 billion in private credit assets in the region.
Partners currently favours high-performing, defensive or less cyclical companies, and is steering away from some of the hottest areas of Asian financing, Bellis said.

Datacentre and GPU financing – which refers to financing to enable companies to acquire advanced technology – is less of a focus, he said, with Partners Group instead targeting “real economy” businesses.
Recent investments have included education and corporate services companies. BLOOMBERG

cna.headline: Shein to pay up to $3.5 billion to select pre-IPO investors around Hong Kong listing
cna.teaser: Shein to pay up to $3.5 billion to select pre-IPO investors around Hong Kong listing
fullText: HONG KONG, Aug 24 : Online fast-fashion retailer Shein will pay up to $3.5 billion to selected existing investors — almost twice the fresh capital it is seeking in an IPO — to help compensate them for a sharp slide in its valuation, its prospectus showed on Monday.

The investors entitled to the payments in cash and extra shares include entities linked to Boyu Capital, Tiger Global, General Atlantic, Thrive Capital, Mubadala, Brookfield and others, the filings showed.
They hold Shein's late-stage funding shares — Series pre-D, Series D and Series D plus preferred — which carry protections triggered by an IPO below the prices paid in earlier funding rounds.
The broader group of preferred shareholders also includes Sanabil Private Equity, Coatue, D1 Capital, DST Asia, Reliance Retail, Coppel Capital, and Claure Group.
The payments are nearly double the up to HK$13.86 billion ($1.77 billion) that Shein aims to raise by selling about 280 million shares in its IPO, based on the top end of its indicated price range.
Shein's proposed IPO price of HK$47.60 to HK$49.50 per share would value the company at up to about $27 billion.

That is below the private valuations attached to the eligible funding rounds of $60.5 billion for the Series pre-D round in 2022, $98.2 billion for the Series D round later that year and $64 billion for the Series D plus round in 2023.

Shein said it could pay up to $2.2 billion in cash under the conversion adjustment protections, assuming the IPO is priced at the bottom of the range. It will also issue 19.6 million additional shares to eligible holders at no cost.
Separately, Shein also agreed to make about $1.33 billion in payments to holders of Series pre-D, D and D plus preferred shares.

That includes about $1.1 billion, payable in three instalments by March 31, June 30 and September 30. A further estimated $230.4 million, which accrues until the IPO closes, will be paid within 15 business days after IPO completion.

Shein said the payments will be funded from its own financial resources. Holders of Shein's older Series A, Series B, Series C and Series C plus preferred shares are not covered, the prospectus showed.

listening.title: Singapore's New Digital Identity Measures to Combat Scams
listening.transcript: As digital banking scams continue to rise in Singapore, major banks are introducing stricter biometric verification steps for high-risk transactions. Starting next month, customers transferring large sums of money will have to use facial scanning technology. While some senior citizens might find this shift challenging, authorities emphasize that these measures are vital to protect personal savings. The Monetary Authority of Singapore hopes this will significantly reduce unauthorized fund transfers.

economistArticle.title: The Limits of Sweet-Talk: Scott Bessent and the Bond Markets
paras: Donald Trump has long desired a Federal Reserve chair who would obediently slash interest rates. In nominating Scott Bessent as Treasury Secretary, he may have found a proxy champion for his monetary ambitions. Bessent, a seasoned hedge-fund manager, has signaled an unconventional strategy: rather than relying on direct monetary levers, he aims to utilize verbal interventions to talk long-term bond yields down, functioning as a de facto market whispering voice.

Bessent’s economic blueprint relies on a combination of deregulation, domestic energy expansion, and fiscal consolidation—dubbed "the three arrows" of his plan. He argues that by projecting a credible commitment to reducing America's federal deficit to 3% of GDP over the coming years, he can induce bond vigilantes to lower borrowing costs. This shadow monetary policy seeks to ease financial conditions for businesses and homebuyers without needing direct rate cuts from Jerome Powell.

However, this strategy faces severe skepticism from Wall Street. The bond market is not easily swayed by political promises, particularly when Trump’s broader agenda is highly inflationary. The prospect of sweeping tariffs, massive tax cuts, and immigration curbs threatens to push prices upward, forcing the Fed to keep interest rates elevated. Bond yields have already marched steadily higher, reflecting deep anxieties about expanding fiscal deficits.

To make matters more complicated, any attempt to talk yields down without concrete, painful spending cuts will likely be interpreted by investors as mere political theater. Modern bond markets demand hard structural discipline over rhetorical flourishes. If Bessent tries to strongarm the market through optimistic projections alone, he risks losing credibility, which could trigger a sharper sell-off in US Treasuries.

Ultimately, Bessent's appointment represents a high-stakes gamble on market psychology. Trump may believe he has found a Treasury chief capable of executing monetary magic from the sidelines. But the hard reality of macroeconomic arithmetic suggests that verbal persuasion cannot substitute for structural policy consistency. The global bond market, stubborn and unyielding, remains the ultimate arbiter of America's fiscal destiny.
economistArticle.cn:
唐纳德·特朗普长期以来一直渴望有一位能够乖乖降息的美联储主席。在提名斯科特·贝森特担任财政部长时，他可能为自己的货币野心找到了一个代理人。贝森特是一位经验丰富的对冲基金经理，他表现出了一种非传统的策略：不依赖直接的货币杠杆，而是旨在利用口头干预来劝说长期债券收益率下降，充当事实上的市场‘低语者’。

贝森特的经济蓝图依赖于放松管制、国内能源扩张和财政紧缩的结合——这被称为他计划的“三支箭”。他认为，通过展现出在未来几年将美国联邦赤字缩减至GDP之3%的可靠承诺，他可以诱导‘债券卫士’降低借贷成本。这种影子货币政策旨在为企业和购房者缓解金融状况，而无需杰罗姆·鲍威尔领导的美联储进行直接降息。

然而，这一策略面临着华尔街的严峻质疑。债券市场绝非易受政治承诺左右之辈，尤其是当特朗普更广泛的议程具有高度通胀性时。彻底关税、大规模减税和限制移民的前景威胁着将物价推高，迫使美联储维持高利率。债券收益率已经稳步攀升，反映出市场对财政赤字扩大的深度焦虑。

更复杂的是，任何在没有具体、痛苦的开支削减的情况下试图劝低收益率的企图，都可能被投资者解读为纯粹的政治作秀。现代债券市场需要硬性的结构性纪律，而非辞藻的修饰。如果贝森特仅仅试图通过乐观的预测来强压市场，他将面临失去信誉的风险，这可能会引发美国国债更急剧的抛售。

归根结底，贝森特的任命代表着对市场心理的一次高风险赌博。特朗普可能认为自己找到了一个能够在场外施展货币魔法的财政掌门人。但宏观经济算术的残酷现实表明，口头说服无法替代结构性政策的一致性。全球债券市场顽固而毫不妥协，依然是美国财政命运的最终仲裁者。
